title: Pravda Replikanta — Engineering Edition
lead: Two research results on motion safety and grasp reliability, with laboratory metrics rather than production claims.

news.title: VLA-Stem separates obstacle response from the VLA policy
news.summary: A local obstacle-response controller augments a VLA without retraining its base model.
news.details: Action chunks become reference trajectories; a local policy adjusts them using robot state and nearby obstacles.
news.technical_novelty: Teacher–student distillation and curriculum learning train the corrective layer.
news.engineering_impact: Safety response can be tested separately from task-selection capability.
news.limitations: Across six constrained simulations, collision-free success reached 52.8% versus 23.7% for the strongest safety baseline; industrial reliability is not established.
news.evidence_status: Research preprint with author-run simulation and hardware tests; no independent replication reported.
news.body:
A VLA model may select a sensible task yet respond poorly to a sudden obstacle. VLA-Stem leaves the base model intact and adds a fast local controller. It receives a motion reference and adapts it using robot state and nearby obstacles.

Across six simulated settings, 52.8% of tasks finished without collision versus 23.7% for the strongest safety comparison. The authors also report fewer collisions in hardware tests. Reproduction requires detailed sensor, controller and scenario settings; this is not a safety certification.

news.title: DexSafe measures object drops alongside dexterity
news.summary: A LEAP hand learns to reposition objects within its fingers; an additional filter reduces drops.
news.details: Training takes place in simulation without human demonstrations, followed by transfer to a real hand with pose sensing or wrist depth vision.
news.technical_novelty: A residual safety filter trades off target-pose accuracy against preserving contact.
news.engineering_impact: Grasp benchmarks should track dropped objects as well as target accuracy.
news.limitations: Over 13.3 hours and more than 4,800 unseen goals on four objects, the base policy reached 95.2% within 2 cm and 0.4 rad; the filter reduced drops by 75% while reaching 91.5%.
news.evidence_status: Preprint with author-run physical experiments; transfer to other hands and objects is not established.
news.body:
Dexterous grasping means more than picking something up: the fingers must move it without letting go. Researchers trained a LEAP hand in simulation, transferred the policy to hardware, and added a safety filter that can favor holding the object over a risky maneuver.

Over 13.3 hours of testing, more than 4,800 unseen target poses were attempted on four objects. The base policy reached 95.2% within tolerance, while the filter cut drops by 75% and retained 91.5% goal attainment. Sensor choices, hand geometry and object distribution remain important to reproducibility.

technology_signal.title: Safety becomes a separately trained capability
technology_signal.summary: Both VLA-Stem and DexSafe add corrective logic around a base task policy.
technology_signal.implications: Engineers should measure collisions, drops and test conditions alongside task success.
